You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Overnight contract desk is `/app/bin/seamwick`. Source fixes under `/app` are required for the pipeline directories named from `/app/opsleaf/MAP.txt`. A static or hand-written blot is not enough. Drive `nudge` and `flood` so `/app/blot/last.json` is produced by the mill. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/seamwick nudge`, `/app/bin/seamwick flood`, and `/app/bin/seamwick sheet` as listed in `/app/opsleaf/VERBS.txt`. Keys for `/app/blot/last.json` are written in `/app/opsleaf/SHEET.txt`. Notes sit under `/app/opsleaf`.

`nudge` still returns 0 after `/app/corpus` tightened a published type. `flood` on that same tree records a finding on a path that `nudge` left out of assayed. Opening that path alone still reports the finding. `/app/blot/last.json` holds assayed, findings, and code. Each findings object has unit, kind, and note. unit is the path under `/app/corpus`. kind is `arity` for a call whose argument count differs from the published type. note is the call name. code is a decimal integer written as text. If `nudge` and `flood` would not share findings, or if assayed skipped a path `flood` would flag, `nudge` must return nonzero. Dirty trees leave findings as a nonempty array. On a `nudge` for a single tightened published type, assayed must not include a path that does not name that type and that `flood` would not flag. A unit that names that type only as a same-package identifier belongs in assayed. A later tightened type following a previous `flood` still has to share findings with `flood`.

`sheet` prints the current blot. assayed, findings, and code are the named keys.

The implementation is Java source under the three MAP-listed directories (purlbox, knitwell, tintlag), with orchestration source in seamcmd and scanning source in impgraph. steps.message:
Analysis: The cache confirms the core issue: Cite records only explicit imports, so api/Vest.u (same-package Bond) and desk/Clerk.u (fully qualified api.Bond) have empty citations. Sched then selects only changed files/importers, and Seal reduces assayed to hit units while its code logic can incorrectly remain 0. The required fixes likely belong precisely in the three MAP-listed generators: purlbox/Cite for type naming, knitwell/Sched for selection, and tintlag/Seal for assay/code invariants. The combined source output was truncated, so exact Drive/Loom data flow still needs targeted inspection.
Plan: Inspect Bag, Loom, Drive, Flood, and generated classes in full with line numbers. Then update each of the three generator sources to: detect all meaningful references to known published types (imports, qualified names, and same-package identifiers); select units citing changed types; retain the correctly analysed set in assayed while avoiding unrelated clean paths; and return nonzero whenever nudge coverage/findings can disagree with flood. Rebuild and reset from seed to test the original tightened-type scenario.

steps.message:
Analysis: Drive computes changedTypes from cached versus current published fingerprints and passes freshly computed citations into Sched. Therefore generator-only fixes are sufficient. Cite should recognize any identifier occurrence, including same-package and qualified references. Sched should include every unit citing a changed type. Seal should preserve all analysed units as assayed and emit nonzero for findings or incomplete mandatory coverage. This makes nudge inspect Bond plus all Bond-naming consumers, exclude unrelated clean Kin/LocalAid, and produce the same two findings as flood.
Plan: Replace the three MAP-listed generators with corrected implementations, rebuild generated classes, restore the seed corpus/cache to recreate the pre-tightening state, and run nudge. Then independently restore the same seed state and run flood so their findings can be compared fairly. Also test opening api/Vest.u alone conceptually via the normal mill behavior and validate sheet/JSON.
